elements.content: Master the core scientific vocabulary and collocations for this topic (10 items):

items.definition: the mental power to store and recall past experiences.
items.example: A good memory is essential for learning new vocabulary.

items.definition: existing in a material or physical form; real and solid.
items.example: Apple' is a concrete noun, while 'love' is abstract.

items.definition: existing as an idea or quality, not a physical object.
items.example: Freedom' is an abstract concept that is hard to visualize.

items.definition: to bring a fact or memory back into one's mind.
items.example: I struggled to recall his phone number in the emergency.
Creating a visual image of a word helps you remember it.

items.definition: a mental connection between ideas, words, or things.
items.example: We have a strong association between red and danger.

items.definition: a word used to identify any of a class of people, places, or things.
items.example: Concrete nouns are much easier for language learners.

items.definition: well known from long or close association.
items.example: He felt comfortable because the settings were familiar.

items.definition: a scientific procedure undertaken to make a discovery.
items.example: The university conducted an experiment on word memory.

items.definition: a consequence or outcome of an action or process.
items.example: The experiment's result proved that concrete words are memorable.

elements.text: Researchers conducted in-depth investigations and empirical trials to analyze these phenomena. The findings reveal critical mechanisms that challenge earlier assumptions.
elements.takeaway: Understanding both biological and empirical evidence allows us to draw more grounded conclusions.
